turns.t: Sorry, G'day, we're here about Jack's arm. He got stung by a bee, and it went huge. Or was it a wasp? I don't know, he's not sure either.
No worries. Jack, how old are you, mate? ~
Seven. ~
Seven, great. Jack, where did the sting get you?
Here. On my arm. It got big.
And when was it?
Two days ago. It was on Wednesday.
No, mate, it's been four days, it was the weekend, at the barbecue. We went to the park on Saturday.
So Jack says two days and Mum says four days, I'll put that as two to four days. How big did it get, Mum?
The whole forearm, red and swollen, like a balloon. It was the size of a sausage roll, honestly.
Any trouble breathing when it happened?
No, nothing like that. He was just crying about the arm.
Any hives anywhere else on his body?
No. Only the arm.
Did he vomit, or go floppy or dizzy?
No. No vomiting, he was running around an hour later.
Any allergies that you know of, to anything?
No, none that we know of. He's been fine with everything.
Has Jack had any operations?
He had grommets put in his ears when he was three.
Does he play outside a lot?
All the time, footy, cricket, the creek. He's a feral.
Let me look at the arm.
It's still a bit pink and swollen, about five centimetres across, near the elbow, but it's going down, and there's no sign of infection.
Is it an allergic reaction? ~
This is what we call a big local reaction, where the swelling stays at the site. It's not the dangerous kind that affects the whole body. ~
That's a relief. ~
Weight 24 kilos and a pulse of 90, all fine.
Should we be worried about next time? ~
Reactions like this don't usually get worse, but I'd like to be thorough. I'd like to arrange a skin test for venom, and a blood test for venom antibodies, at the specialist clinic.
Is that needed? ~
I'd like to rule out a bigger problem, and it gives us a plan for next time. ~
Okay. ~
Meanwhile, if he's stung again, wash the area, give a cold pack, and if there's any trouble breathing, swelling of his face, or he goes pale or floppy, call 000.
Got it. ~
I'd like to see you again in six weeks, once those tests are done.
Six weeks. Thanks, doc. ~
